title: Turkish F-16s Strike Al-Shabaab Riverbank Positions in Basra as Ground Fighting Continues
detail: Turkish F-16 fighter jets, operating out of Mogadishu's Aden Adde International Airport, carried out airstrikes on August 31, 2026 against Al-Shabaab positions along the riverbank in Basra, Middle Shabelle, where Somali government forces have been battling the group for about a week (see the Aug 30 report of fighting entering its sixth day). Local sources reported heavy casualties among the militants, though the toll was not independently verified, and neither Ankara nor Mogadishu issued an official statement confirming the strikes, their targets, or casualties. The strikes mark a further escalation of Turkey's direct air support for Somali ground operations near the capital.

media.caption: Turkish F-16s struck Al-Shabaab riverbank positions in Basra, near Mogadishu, Aug 31, 2026

title: Puntland President Accuses Foreign Powers of Using Anti-Piracy Pretext to Exploit Marine Resources
detail: Speaking in Garacad on August 31, 2026, Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni accused unnamed foreign powers of using the piracy resurgence as a pretext to gain access to Puntland's marine resources, saying: 'The intention is to extract our resources through deploying forces to our coast under the guise that Puntland has failed to defend itself from piracy.' Deni rejected unilateral foreign military intervention along Puntland's coast, citing concern over civilian casualties from international operations and referencing past resource depletion during earlier eras of heavy foreign naval presence. The remarks come amid an active hostage crisis in which the IMO says more than 90 seafarers remain held across multiple hijacked vessels, including the tanker MT Honour 25.

media.caption: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni speaking in Garacad, Aug 31, 2026, rejecting foreign intervention on Puntland's coast

title: Puntland and AFRICOM Discuss Proposed US Base in Bosaso and Maritime Security Cooperation
detail: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni met with AFRICOM officials led by Col. James Rose in Bosaso on August 31, 2026 to discuss establishing a US military base in the city, joint counterterrorism operations against ISIS-Somalia in Puntland's Golis/Cal Miskaad mountain ranges, and counter-piracy and naval training cooperation. Puntland officials stressed that any counter-piracy, maritime security or airstrike operations along its coast 'should not proceed without its knowledge and cooperation' — a pointed rebuke aimed at Turkey's uncoordinated coastal counter-piracy activity and coming the same day Deni publicly warned against foreign powers using piracy as a pretext to access Puntland's marine resources.

media.caption: Puntland President Deni met AFRICOM officials in Bosaso to discuss a proposed US base and maritime security cooperation, Aug 31, 2026

title: Somalia and AU Race to Secure AUSSOM Funding Ahead of UN Security Council Summit
detail: Somalia and the African Union are scrambling to secure funding for AUSSOM ahead of an upcoming UN Security Council summit, Garowe Online reported August 31, 2026, as the mission's financial and troop base erodes on multiple fronts — the US funding cutoff after AUSSOM's December 31, 2026 mandate expiry, the UNSOS drawdown already underway, and Uganda's August 28 announcement that it will fully withdraw its troops by August 2027. Mogadishu is pursuing bilateral deals with individual troop-contributing countries such as Uganda, which controls the Halane base near Mogadishu's airport, to keep forces present outside formal AU funding structures, while outreach to Arab nations for financial support has 'fallen short of what is needed.' The government now concedes AUSSOM will be needed through at least 2028, a reversal of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's October 2022 pledge to remove all foreign troops from Somalia by December 2024.

media.caption: Somalia and the AU are racing to secure AUSSOM funding ahead of a UN Security Council summit, reported Aug 31, 2026
